extracted.intended_audience: researchers who have not yet reviewed and researchers seeking training in peer review (e.g., early-career researchers, prospective reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: A directed self-learning course designed to teach researchers how to conduct and write helpful peer review reports, handle ethical issues, understand peer review models and processes, and make editorial recommendations. The course includes core modules required for certification plus optional elements to suit individual learning needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of the peer review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Understanding of the peer review process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers what peer review is and why it exists (module 1.1), models of peer review (module 1.2), and the typical peer review process (module 1.3). Fundamental knowledge expected before undertaking reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on writing a helpful peer review report
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on writing a helpful peer review report
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses how to structure and compose reports reviewers submit to authors and editors (see module 3.1). Implies emphasis on producing useful, clear feedback but the course materials provide the specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advice on handling ethical issues concerning peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice on handling ethical issues concerning peer review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers ethical considerations relevant to reviewing (conflict of interest, confidentiality, plagiarism, inappropriate behavior). Learners are guided on recognising and responding to ethical problems in the review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Models of peer review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains different peer review models (module content). Useful for choosing appropriate conduct depending on whether review is single-blind, double-blind, open, etc.; content acts as descriptive guidance rather than prescriptive rules for every journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: The typical peer review process
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers the standard lifecycle of a manuscript submission through editorial handling and reviewer input (module content). Helps reviewers understand timing, roles, and expected deliverables at each stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to get involved (becoming a reviewer)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance on practical steps to become a peer reviewer: how to be invited, how to present credentials, networking/approach to editors (module content).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to a review invitation / initial decision to accept
rubrics_metrics.description: 2.0 I just got a review invite, what’s next?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module covering immediate actions on receiving an invitation (assessing fit, conflicts, time availability, scope). Implies criteria for accepting/declining and initial communications with editors.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to write a helpful peer review report (detailed module)
rubrics_metrics.description: 3.1 How to write a helpful peer review report
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dedicated webinar (module 3.1) that provides practical advice on drafting the review text reviewers give authors: structure, tone, level of detail and focus. The course provides examples and exercises but allows flexibility by journal/editor context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comments to editors and decision recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: 3.2 The comments to editors and decision recommendations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific guidance on what to include in private comments to editors and how to make clear, justified recommendations (accept, minor/major revision, reject). Emphasises discriminating between confidential editorial advice and comments for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to peer review a review article
rubrics_metrics.description: 3.3 How to peer review a review article
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Module focusing on the specific criteria and expectations when reviewing review/synthesis articles (e.g., comprehensiveness, balance, currency of references, structure).

rubrics_metrics.name: Course orientation and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: What to expect from the Certified Peer Reviewer Course?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short orientation content (module) setting out time commitment (total 3+ hours), module completion, and outcomes so learners know the level of engagement required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core-module completion required for certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Several core modules must be completed to gain certification
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The course contains required core modules and optional modules; certification requires completion of the specified core modules (exact modules identified in the syllabus).

rubrics_metrics.name: Directed self-learning and modular flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Delivered via directed self-learning in the form of webinars, podcasts and questionnaires; pick and choose additional elements to suit individual learning needs and interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Course is asynchronous and modular — learners can select optional content. This affects how training is applied and indicates different depths of competency depending on modules completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt reviews to journal/editor-specific instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Practices, requirements, instructions and methodologies can vary considerably according to the context in which you are working, the type of journal and the specific editor and title so the examples and suggestions in the course should be taken as illustrative but non-exhaustive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit instruction to refer to a journal’s guide for authors and any specific instructions or advice from the editor or journal for the most relevant instructions for your review. Certification content is illustrative and must be adapted to local editorial policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification is not a guarantee of reviewer selection
rubrics_metrics.description: *Please note that completion of the Certified Peer Reviewer course does not guarantee invitation or selection as a reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that certification signals competence but does not replace editorial selection processes; reviewers should continue to engage with editors and follow journal-specific criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential institutional recognition as continuing professional education
rubrics_metrics.description: Possible that your institution might recognize your certification as evidence of continuing professional education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes an ancillary benefit: certification may be used as CPD evidence depending on employer/institution policies.
